surface: shogiful — /apps/shogiful/ (Persuade) + /apps/shogiful/privacy/, /apps/shogiful/support/ and the six /alternatives/ pages that target it (81dojo, kanazawa-shogi, lishogi, piyoshogi, shogi-quest, shogi-wars) as Read variants

dossier.mechanism: Shogiful runs YaneuraOu on-device over every game you play against its AI opponents, sorts each significant mistake into shogi's own categories (drop, promotion, castle, missed tsume) and states it as one plain-English sentence on a board you can read without kanji. It then drills those same patterns back to you with spaced repetition.
dossier.audienceScene: A Westerner who already plays chess and met shogi through anime, a board-game night or YouTube. It is evening, they are on their phone, and they have just lost to a drop they never saw. They arrive from Google or an AI answer ('shogi app english', 'learn shogi without kanji', 'Shogi Wars alternative'). On desktop they are researching and have to get the app onto their iPhone.
dossier.culturalHome: Shogi culture as a foreigner meets it: public and televised commentary at the big magnetic board (大盤解説), tsume problem books and newspaper columns, the kifu record and Hodges notation (P-7f, S*4e), the club or dojo with its rank tags, kyu/dan ranks and post-game review (感想戦), and shogi manga and anime. On top of that sit the chess player's own habits: annotated games and demonstration boards.
dossier.mustProve: Within the first viewport, show a real kind of shogi mistake explained in one plain sentence ('You dropped the silver to 4d. A knight drop on 3c forked king and rook.') on a board labelled in Western notation. Beside it sit the working App Store badge, the desktop QR and the price statement 'Free — Premium from $1.99/mo'.
dossier.categoryDefault: A dark navy/black page with a gold glow (the register of the app's own 王-koma icon), a 3D wooden board inside an iPhone bezel, kanji everywhere, ink-wash, samurai or sakura cues, a split hero with a badge row, then a grid of feature cards.
dossier.predictableOpposite: Either a bright, flat beginner page led by a mascot (the PiyoShogi-chick or Duolingo register), or a clinical white 'AI coach' SaaS page full of evaluation graphs and accuracy rings.
dossier.literalReading: Shogi-ful read literally gives the wedge-shaped koma on a kaya board (the icon is literally a 王 piece). The headline 'speaks your language' read literally gives translation, subtitles or a phrasebook. Candidate 6 (subtitle track) is the one literal slot among the seven, and none of the three styles uses it.

_data/transparency.yml shogiful: 0 third-party SDKs, 0 tracking domains, no account, analytics none, network calls none to third parties (NNUE file fetched once via Apple On-Demand Resources), optional iCloud sync to your own iCloud, required-reason API UserDefaults CA92.1

Journal 'making-shogi-readable-without-kanji': all 8 pieces share one wedge and are told apart only by kanji. Readability needs identity + movement + promotion state. Behaviour first, symbol second. Western set is the default outside Japanese locales. Hodges/Hosking notation (P-7f, S*4e). Journal 'reading-a-shogi-engine-evaluation': words instead of numbers, eval bands.

Alternatives (shogi-wars, piyoshogi read in full; 81dojo, lishogi, shogi-quest, kanazawa-shogi target it): positioned as 'the practice room, not the arena'; each page has an honest verdict, a 2-column table, FAQ and app card
Privacy page front matter has an seo block; overview / data_collection / data_storage / third_parties (StoreKit, Game Center) / children / changes. Support page has an seo block and slug.

candidates.name: Ōban commentary board (大盤解説)
candidates.why: At every title match a professional stands at a giant vertical magnetic board, slides flat piece plates and explains each move aloud to a hall or a TV audience. That is Shogiful's job done in public, and chess players know the same thing as the demonstration board. It carries the mechanism by making the page one big board on which each worked mistake is replayed with a 'you played' magnet, a 'best was' magnet and one spoken sentence.

candidates.name: Tsume-shogi problem book and newspaper column
candidates.why: Edo-era tsume collections (the roadmap draws on them) and the daily newspaper tsume column are shogi's self-study ritual. It carries the mechanism by setting each of your own mistakes as a numbered problem diagram with the pieces in hand listed and the plain-language answer one fold below.

candidates.name: Kifu record sheet (棋譜用紙)
candidates.why: This is the ruled game-record form the record-keeper fills in pencil, and the annotated-game page every chess player learned from. It carries 'move by move' as the page's structure: your game's move list in Hodges notation runs down the page, and the mistake rows are annotated in sentences in the margin.

candidates.name: 1964 Tokyo pictogram program
candidates.why: Japan built the first modern sports pictogram system (Katsumi Masaru, Yamashita Yoshirō) so visitors who could not read kanji could find their way, which is the same problem Shogiful solves on the board. It carries the Western piece set and its movement indicators as a full pictogram identity on a construction grid that reads without a single character.

candidates.name: Shogi manga explainer chapter
candidates.why: Many Westerners meet shogi through manga and anime (March Comes in Like a Lion has explainer pages), and the English editions keep the Japanese sound effects with small translations beside them. It carries the coaching loop as panels (board, drop, focus lines on the missed square, explanation in a balloon) and carries 'speaks your language' as translated SFX.

candidates.name: English subtitle track
candidates.why: The anime-curious audience watches Japanese with English subtitles. It carries the engine-to-English translation as timed subtitle lines under board stills. It is the literal reading of the headline metaphor, so it takes the single literal slot.

candidates.name: Dojo rank-tag wall (名札掛け)
candidates.why: Shogi clubs (and the martial-arts dojos Westerners know) hang members' wooden name tags under kyu/dan headers and re-hang them on promotion, beside the fee plaques and the posted rules. It carries the 10-opponent ladder (beat each twice to unlock the next), the visitor's own progress, the offer and the house rules (no account, no ads, no clock) as the fixtures of one wall. Of the seven it is the weakest at carrying the explanations.

styles.label: The Club Tag Wall
styles.lineage: The 名札掛け (nafuda-kake) of a Japanese shogi club (将棋道場/将棋センター): hinoki name tags hung on a lacquered rail under kyu/dan header plaques and re-hung on promotion. Around it on the same wall: the seat-fee plaques (席料), the printed house rules, the cork board with review and 次の一手 quiz sheets, the ○△× marks of Japanese evaluation charts, the framed operating licence by the door, and the owner's hanko stamp.
styles.thesis: The page is one club wall read top to bottom. The AI opponents and the visitor's own blank tag hang on a real rank rack, and that rack is also the navigation. The offer hangs as fee plaques and the coaching proof is pinned up as a review notice. It refuses both the category's dark-navy-and-gold 3D-board hero and the split-hero template.
styles.scene: A chess player who has just lost to a drop reads on their phone in the evening, as if standing in front of a neighbourhood shogi club's wall under flat fluorescent tubes: shadowless cool-white light on painted plaster and pale hinoki. The scheme is light only.

type.utility: Yusei Magic 400 (17 KB): the club owner's marker notes on notices, e.g. 'scan with your iPhone camera', 'beat each one twice'
type.rationale: Shippori Mincho B1's ink-pooled heavy mincho reads as sumi lettering on wood, and its Latin holds up stacked upright on narrow tags. The specimen check showed Yuji Syuku's and Yuji Boku's Latin fails at that. BIZ UDPGothic is Morisawa's universal-design gothic used on Japanese municipal and school notices, a public-legibility face that matches the promise of a board anyone can read. Yusei Magic is the magic-marker hand of handwritten club annotations. Total ≈103 KB.

styles.navigation: The top lacquer rail is the rank rail. Its header plaques are the section links (Review · Rack · Method · Rules · Fees · Questions), and the visitor's YOU tag hangs under the plaque of the section in view. On mobile the rail scrolls horizontally with snap, and the active plaque stays scrolled into view. The microsite has no hamburger and no other menu.
styles.signatureInteraction: Re-hang your tag. A hinoki YOU tag with a vermilion edge hangs from the nav rail under the plaque of the section in view. When the section changes, the tag lifts off its nail, slides along the rail and settles with a damped 3° pendulum swing (CSS transform transition; IntersectionObserver sets data-at on the rail). Without JS the tag sits fixed under 'Review' and every plaque is a plain anchor link. Under reduced motion the tag jumps to its new nail with no lift and no swing.
styles.motionGrammar: Only hanging things move: tags and plaques enter by dropping 8px and swinging to rest (420ms, cubic-bezier(.3,1.4,.5,1)). Pinned paper never moves, and body text never fades. There is no parallax and no counters. prefers-reduced-motion removes every entrance and swing.
styles.readModeVariant: Privacy, support and the six alternatives pages are posted documents on the same wall: celadon frame, the same lacquer rail (its first plaque returns to /apps/shogiful/), and the title lettered on a lacquer plank. The reading column is one long paper notice (#F7F6F1), 68ch, BIZ UDPGothic 17/28px ink, pinned with two pins. Privacy: the policy as the notice, with the framed transparency inspection record beside it on desktop and above it on mobile. Support: 'Ask at the desk' with the email lettered on a hinoki plaque, plus response time and what to include. Alternatives: the plank reads e.g. 'Shogiful or Shogi Wars', the comparison is a ○△× posted chart, the verdict is two notices ('Pick Shogiful if…' / 'Pick Shogi Wars if…'), the FAQ is desk cards, and a badge mount sits at the foot.
styles.assetsNeeded: None are required to ship: every fixture is CSS (flat colour, hairlines, clip-path wedges) and runs on the existing icon, screenshots, QR and badge. Owner inputs: (1) the confirmed opponent roster, meaning names, strengths and the four tier labels, because the front matter and screenshot 7 disagree; (2) optionally, the app's Western piece set exported as SVG to replace the Hodges letters on the diagram wedges.
styles.risk: The world carries the ladder and the offer better than the core proof. If the build lets the review notice fall below the first viewport, the page reads as a club with an opponent ladder, which is PiyoShogi's strength rather than Shogiful's. The roster conflict blocks the rack until the owner confirms it. Celadon, hinoki and vermilion slide into Japan-heritage kitsch the moment brush textures, washi or sakura creep in, so the room must stay a fluorescent-lit municipal club. Upright-stacked Latin on tags tops out at about 8 letters.
styles.memoryTest: The shogi app whose page was a club wall: a row of wooden name tags for the AI opponents, and my own blank tag that slid along the rail as I scrolled.

styles.navigation: A slim hall strip with six plain text links, and the active section underlined in board-white. On mobile the 'Programme' button opens a <details> list. Inside Commentary, the board's file labels 9…1 double as a jump list to the six worked examples.
styles.signatureInteraction: Magnet replay. While Commentary is in view, the board is position: sticky. As each worked-example caption reaches the caption slot, the plates slide square to square into that example's illustrative position, which is stored as an SFEN string on the caption in server-rendered HTML. The red 'you played' and green 'best was' arrows then draw in from tail to head. Without JS, every caption renders with its own static board diagram above it, built from the same position data, so nothing is missing. Under reduced motion, positions swap instantly with arrows already drawn.
styles.motionGrammar: Motion is the commentator's hand and nothing else: plates slide in straight lines (180ms ease-out) and land with a 1.04→1 snap, and arrows draw over 240ms. The hall, text and plates never fade or parallax. prefers-reduced-motion turns this into instant state changes.
styles.readModeVariant: The hall is the frame: slate ground, the same strip nav, and the page title in Dela Gothic on the title band. The reading column is one lit plate (#F2F0E8), 68ch, Atkinson 17/28px ink. Privacy: the policy plate with a plain transparency table at its head. Support: one caption plate with the email in Atkinson 700 24px and the response time. Alternatives: the title band reads e.g. 'Shogiful or PiyoShogi', with an optional small board diagram. The comparison table and the honest verdict are plain text on the plate, the FAQ is 'Questions from the floor', and the badge strip sits at the foot.
styles.assetsNeeded: Six illustrative positions (SFEN), one per worked example. They must be authored, checked with an engine and labelled 'illustrative position'. Optional: the app's Western piece set as SVG to replace the Hodges letters on plates. Otherwise it runs on the existing icon, screenshots, QR and badge.
styles.risk: It is familiar: a big board is what every chess and shogi page leads with, and many runs land here. It earns its place only if the board is real HTML with moving magnets and captions, never a picture. Sticky scrollytelling is fragile on mobile (address-bar resize, iOS sticky jank) and has to fall back cleanly to stacked diagram-plus-caption pairs. A wrong illustrative position is a factual error any shogi player will spot. The dark hall sits near the dark-plus-accent cluster, so the lit board must stay the dominant light.
styles.memoryTest: A huge white shogi board I could read without kanji. As I scrolled, the magnets moved, red for what I did and green for what I should have done, with one plain sentence underneath.

styles.label: Weekly Manga Chapter
styles.lineage: A shogi manga chapter as printed in Japanese weekly magazines and their English editions: the colour opening page (巻頭カラー), panel grids with slanted gutters, speech balloons and narration boxes, screentone, 集中線 focus lines, and Japanese sound effects (パチッ, the snap of a piece on the board) kept in the art with small English translations beside them. It also borrows the yonkoma strip, the obi band and the 奥付 colophon. The explainer pages of shogi manga such as March Comes in Like a Lion are a cultural reference only; no art, characters or logos are borrowed.
styles.thesis: The page is one manga chapter read top to bottom. The coaching loop is told in panels: a board panel, the drop, focus lines slamming into the square you missed, and the explanation in a balloon. The English edition's translated SFX carry 'the teacher that speaks your language'. It refuses both the luxury wood-and-gold board page and the flat infographic.
styles.scene: A reader on an evening commuter train flipping through a weekly manga magazine printed on tinted newsprint under the carriage's daylight-white lights. The scheme is light (the colour opener uses the app's navy as a printed colour page).

type.rationale: Potta One's brush-pop strokes read as hand-lettered manga titling, and its Latin carries the same hand as the katakana SFX. Zen Old Mincho is the old-style mincho of tankōbon body text with a sound Latin, so long reading stays calm. Shantell Sans in caps stands in for the comic lettering of English manga editions. The katakana SFX ship as outlined SVG paths rather than a Japanese font subset. Total ≈102 KB.

styles.navigation: A table of contents (目次). The navy top bar's 'Contents' link opens a full-height contents page as a <details> panel, so it works without JS, listing the sections by their in-world names. On desktop the six main entries also sit inline in the bar. The change of newsprint stock signals which signature you are in, and every section heading is a Potta One title in a narration box.
styles.signatureInteraction: Focus-line drop. When a board panel enters the viewport, the 集中線 contract toward the missed square (a CSS custom property animating the mask radius), the dropped piece plate cuts in, and the パチッ SFX outline draws on (SVG stroke-dashoffset) with its English gloss appearing beside it. The balloon cuts in last. Without JS, the server-rendered final state shows lines, plate, SFX, gloss and balloon all present. Under reduced motion the final state is static.
styles.motionGrammar: Cuts, not tweens: panel contents appear in reading order with hard cuts 120ms apart, like turning to the next panel. Only the focus lines (300ms) and SFX strokes (250ms) animate continuously, and nothing fades or uses parallax. prefers-reduced-motion shows everything at once.
styles.readModeVariant: Privacy, support and the alternatives pages are the volume's back matter. Each uses one newsprint frame (sky for privacy, pink for support, lemon for alternatives) with the title in Potta One on a narration box. The reading column is a white notes page at 68ch in Zen Old Mincho 18/30 ink. An alternatives page opens with one 'versus' panel in which two balloons quote each product's real positioning from the page ('the arena' / 'the practice room'). The comparison table and verdict follow as plain text, the FAQ as reader Q&A, and the okuzuke colophon closes the page.
styles.assetsNeeded: Katakana SFX outlined as SVG paths (パチッ at minimum; derived from an OFL face), plus six illustrative board crops (positions) labelled 'illustrative position'. Optional: the app's Western piece set as SVG. Focus lines, screentone and stocks are all CSS, and it otherwise runs on the existing icon, screenshots, QR and badge. No character art is needed or allowed.
styles.risk: To a serious chess convert, manga can read as 'for kids and anime fans'. Caps comic lettering hurts long reading, so balloons must stay headline-short and all long copy must live in mincho narration. With no drawn characters, panels can look like diagrams in boxes, so the focus lines, SFX and balloons have to carry the drama. Drenched stocks tip into noise if colour changes per panel rather than per signature. The SFX must be correct Japanese and glossed. IP care: generic manga grammar only.
styles.memoryTest: The shogi app page that was a manga: focus lines slamming into the square where I should have dropped my knight, a huge パチッ with '(snap)' beside it, and pink and yellow newsprint pages.

canon: Category standard played straight: a dark navy App Store landing page with the gold 王 icon, a 3D wooden board in an iPhone bezel beside the headline, a badge row, a feature-card grid, a pricing table and an FAQ accordion.
notes: The roll ran degraded (no catalog challengers, no quality-bar boards), as expected; the network was not retried. Seed c0f5a51b: assigned 7, which maps to A, THE ROLL (Dojo rank-tag wall). Re-roll 1 gave 5, which maps to C, SECOND ROLL (manga chapter). Neither is 1, so B is my top-ranked candidate 1 (ōban commentary board) as IMPECCABLE’S PICK, and its risk line names its familiarity. The seven candidates span 6 material families, and the one literal slot (6, subtitles) was not dealt. Truth flags for the owner: (1) The opponent roster in the front matter (10 opponents, Hana ~500 to Sensei ~1800, 4 tiers) contradicts screenshots 7 and 4 (Koishi…Kaede, Kiri 1,400, Inazuma). Every style names opponents only after confirmation, and A depends on it most. (2) No asset shows the Western piece set, since all screenshots show kanji. All diagrams use Hodges letters on CSS wedges labelled 'Western notation', and an SVG export of the app's set is an optional upgrade. (3) All six board positions are illustrative and must be labelled as such. (4) The 'Targeted 2026 Q3' roadmap item has passed (today 2026-10-05) and renders with its disclaimer; the owner may want to refresh it. (5) The founder signal '19 live apps' is a literal in the front matter and must be kept in sync, while new copy computes the count. (6) Ratings count is 14, so no stars appear anywhere. Font budgets were checked against Fontsource latin files: A ≈103 KB, B ≈47 KB, C ≈102 KB. A specimen render ruled out Yuji Syuku and Yuji Boku as tag faces because their Latin is weak. Contrast pairs were computed and are listed in the palette roles. A's headline sits on a lacquer plank, not a hinoki plank, to keep it out of the cream-plus-serif cluster.
